evaluationCost.note: evaluation cost; never added to arm cost

evidence.quote: | true, days when days >= 1 && days <= 365 -> Ok(Some(NetEndOfMonth days))

ARC-REV-01.rationale: Every new rule is in Tier 1 or Tier 2. The new terms case and the end-of-month due-date rule are in Summa.Ledger (Tier 1). The form's parsing and its 1 to 365 range are in Summa.Web.Engine (Tier 2). Storage (Tier 2) only encodes and decodes the value. The change touches no Tier 3 or Tier 4 code.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No effect is added. The due date is computed from the issue date passed in, and DateTime.DaysInMonth is a pure calendar function, not a clock read. The form's parsing is a pure transition, and the storage codec turns values into data without doing I/O.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The wording 'Net N EOM' is written twice, once in Documents.termsText and once in the audit trail's Invoicing.termsWords, instead of being defined once and reused. The two copies match today but could drift apart. This follows the existing pattern for 'Net {days}'. The due-date rule and the stored 'net-eom' encoding are each defined once.

evidence.quote: | true, day when day >= 1 && day <= 28 -> Ok(Some(DayOfNextMonth day))

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The new terms case, the due-date rule, the ordinal wording and the terms text are all in Summa.Ledger (Tier 1). The form's 'day N' parsing and its 1 to 28 range are in the Tier 2 engine. No Tier 3 or Tier 4 code is touched. Ledger does not enforce the 1 to 28 range itself; only the engine and decoding check it. But no higher tier decides the range, so this does not lower the score.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No effect is added. dueDate uses only the issue date (AddMonths) and DateOnly construction. The parsing and the storage codec are pure.

evidence.quote: let dayOfNextMonthText (day: int) = $"Due the {ordinal day} of next month"

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The new wording is defined once, in dayOfNextMonthText with ordinal. Both termsText and the audit trail's termsWords call it. The due-date rule and the 'day-of-next-month' encoding are each defined once. The 1 to 28 range is checked only in the engine's parsing. The change set does not touch the 'Net N EOM' copies from change set 1, so they do not count here.
